etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Italian, from Neapolitan lava (“lava”, but also “downpour overflowing the streets”). Likely in the sense of “landslide, torrent” from Latin labes (“fall”), compare labina (“avalanche, landslide”). A supposed relation with lavare (“to wash”) is now widely discredited. Neither is there probably any relation with Arabic لابة (lāba, “black volcanic rock”). (Can this etymology be sourced?)

definitions.definition: The molten rock ejected by a volcano from its crater or fissured sides; magma that has breached the surface of the earth.
A shade of red, named after the volcanic lava.
